technical_source_policy: primary papers or author-hosted mathematical notes only; no novelty claim

sources.title: Importance sampling the union of rare events with an application to power systems analysis
sources.authors: Art B. Owen, Yury Maximov, Michael Chertkov
sources.version: arXiv:1710.06965v4, revised 19 December 2018; Electronic Journal of Statistics 13 (2019), 231-254
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The paper explicitly conditions Gaussian inputs on a selected constituent halfspace, mixes events proportional to their marginal probabilities, and corrects the count of events occurring in each sample. It identifies earlier Karp-Luby and Gaussian-exceedance methods. Its bounded event-multiplicity estimator is the direct prior method underlying our example.
sources.used_for: Strongest same-input classical control and novelty failure; exact conditional Gaussian sampling formula

sources.title: Weighted Average Importance Sampling and Defensive Mixture Distributions
sources.retrieved_evidence_ranges: Publisher/search abstract; direct publisher open later returned an internal error
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The abstract explains that including the target density in the importance mixture bounds the weights. The weight bound used here is also proved directly in PROOF.txt.
sources.used_for: Defensive-mixture prior art only, with direct algebraic proof independent of source access

sources.title: Math 774 - Credit Risk Modeling
sources.authors: M. R. Grasselli and T. R. Hurd
sources.retrieved_evidence_ranges: Appendix A.10, printed pp.125-126, Proposition A.10.1
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The notes give the finite-horizon maximum/minimum laws for Brownian motion with constant drift and explain their derivation by reflection followed by a Gaussian measure change. The environmental localization proof uses that classical formula after an exact discrete Gaussian martingale embedding.
sources.used_for: Cross-check of the drifted Brownian crossing formula; the discrete Euler localization construction is reconstructed in PROOF.txt

sources.title: Subsolutions of an Isaacs Equation and Efficient Schemes for Importance Sampling
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The abstract describes dynamic importance sampling via classical subsolutions and analyzes asymptotic efficiency. We did not use it as proof of any finite-sample residual bound for the inherited guide.
sources.used_for: Existing subsolution-method context, not a premise of our certificates
